class.name: PerformanceRecorder
class.brief_description: Records per-frame performance metrics into a ring buffer and a CSV file.

method.name: add_metric
method.description: Adds [param delta] to the metric [param id]. For a [constant METRIC_COUNTER] the sum is recorded and reset to [code]0[/code] after each row. A gauge that was never set starts from [code]0[/code]. Lock-free and thread-safe.

method.name: flush
method.description: Writes all rows that are not written yet to the CSV file at once, ignoring [member PerformanceRecordingProfile.flush_budget_usec]. Works while recording and after [method stop]. With [member PerformanceRecordingProfile.flush_interval_frames] set to [code]0[/code], this writes the last [member PerformanceRecordingProfile.buffer_frames] rows. Emits [signal flushed] if rows were written. Returns [constant ERR_UNCONFIGURED] if there is no output path, and [constant ERR_FILE_CANT_WRITE] if the file cannot be written.

method.name: get_column
method.description: Returns the values of the column [param name] that are still in the ring buffer, oldest first: the last [member PerformanceRecordingProfile.buffer_frames] rows at most. Missing values are [constant @GDScript.NAN]. The data stays available after [method stop] until the next [method start]. Useful for in-game graphs.

method.name: get_column_names
method.description: Returns the names of the columns of the current (or last) recording, in CSV order: builtins, [Performance] monitors, custom monitors, metric sources ([code]source/value[/code]), then pushed metrics.

method.name: get_metric_id
method.description: Returns the id of the metric [param name], or [code]-1[/code] if it is not registered.

method.name: get_output_path
method.description: Returns the path of the CSV file of the current (or last) recording, with the placeholders replaced. Returns an empty string if the rows stay in memory only.

method.name: get_recorded_frame_count
method.description: Returns the number of rows recorded since [method start], including rows that are no longer in the ring buffer.

method.name: has_metric_source
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if a native metric source called [param name] is registered. Metric sources are registered by engine modules in C++, for example the .NET runtime metrics.

method.name: register_metric
method.description: Registers a metric that the game pushes with [method set_metric] or [method add_metric], and returns its id. If [param name] is already registered, its id is returned and its kind is set to [param kind]. At most 256 metrics can be registered; returns [code]-1[/code] if the limit is reached. Metrics registered while recording get a column from the next [method start]. Thread-safe.

method.name: set_metric
method.description: Sets the value of the metric [param id]. The value is recorded in the next row. Lock-free and thread-safe.

method.name: start
method.description: Starts recording with [param profile], or with a new [PerformanceRecordingProfile] (default columns) if [param profile] is [code]null[/code]. A running recording is stopped first. Allocates the ring buffer, creates missing directories of the output path and emits [signal recording_started]. The CSV file is created at the first write.

method.name: stop
method.description: Stops recording, writes all remaining rows to the CSV file and emits [signal recording_stopped]. The engine also writes the remaining rows when it quits normally.

signal.name: flushed
signal.description: Emitted on the main thread after [param rows] rows were appended to the CSV file. A flush split over several frames emits it once per frame.

signal.name: recording_stopped
signal.description: Emitted by [method stop] after the remaining rows are written. [param path] is the CSV file, or an empty string if nothing was written.

constants.constant: Column [code]frame_time[/code]: microseconds the engine spent on this frame (physics, process and rendering), without the wait for the next frame.
Column [code]process_time[/code]: microseconds spent in process and rendering this frame.
Column [code]physics_time[/code]: microseconds of the longest physics step of this frame ([code]0[/code] if no step ran).
Column [code]physics_steps[/code]: number of physics steps in this frame.

Column [code]process_memory[/code]: memory used by the process in bytes ([method OS.get_process_memory_usage]), read every [member PerformanceRecordingProfile.process_memory_interval_frames] frames. Empty if the platform cannot report it.
Column [code]process_memory_peak[/code]: highest [code]process_memory[/code] value read since recording started. For the peak of the whole process, see [method OS.get_process_memory_info].

Column [code]gpu_time[/code]: GPU time of the root viewport in milliseconds ([method RenderingServer.viewport_get_measured_render_time_gpu]). The measurement is enabled on the root viewport while recording and disabled by [method stop]. The value is from the latest frame whose GPU results are available, usually a few frames earlier. [code]0[/code] with the Compatibility renderer and on Web.
Column [code]recorder_time[/code]: microseconds the recorder spent on this row, including the CSV writes done since the previous row. Use it to check the cost of a recording.
Represents the size of the [enum Builtin] enum.
The metric keeps its value until it is set again, for example a number of enemies.
The metric is reset to [code]0[/code] after each recorded row, so a row holds what was added since the previous row, for example spawned enemies.
